title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Brunei: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a citizen of Brunei Darussalam is facing a serious or life-limiting illness, putting healthcare communication, registered Powers of Attorney, SPK retirement nominations, and dual-system succession paperwork in place while legal capacity remains intact avoids court delays and protects household finances. Under Brunei's civil and Syariah legal systems, Powers of Attorney must be formally registered with the Attorney General's Chambers to take effect locally, while advance medical preferences are recorded through hospital care teams rather than a standalone living-will statute. This guide sets out the key administrative steps from Brunei statutes and official institutions [1][3][4].

steps.title: Palliative care services and medical coordination
steps.html:
• Hospital specialist and palliative clinics: Coordinate treatment goals, home-nursing referrals, and pain-management plans through government hospitals (such as Raja Isteri Pengiran Anak Saleha Hospital) under Ministry of Health (MOH) Brunei Darussalam [1].
  • Universal citizen health coverage and Bru-HIMS records: Confirm that your family member's Brunei Identity Card and Bru-HIMS health record number are kept current for public specialist clinics, prescriptions, and community palliative visits [1].
  • Medical certification for benefits: Request clear specialist summaries of diagnosis, functional capacity, and prognosis early, as both retirement scheme early withdrawals and legal capacity proceedings rely on formal medical evidence [1][4].

steps.title: Advance care planning and medical decision-making
steps.html:
• Recorded clinical preferences: Brunei has no standalone statutory living-will or advance medical directive act, so patients document treatment values, comfort-care goals, and preferred care location directly with their treating physicians in hospital notes [1].
  • Prohibition on assisted dying: Both Brunei's civil legal framework and Islamic Syariah principles prohibit euthanasia and assisted suicide; clinical care focuses on proportionate symptom control and palliative support [1].
  • Designating a family medical contact: Identify the primary next-of-kin spokesperson in hospital files while the ill person retains capacity so medical teams know whom to update during inpatient care [1].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney and mental capacity safeguards
steps.html:
• Mandatory deposit at the AGC Registry: To take legal effect within Brunei Darussalam, a Power of Attorney must be attested and deposited with the Registry of Powers of Attorney at Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) Brunei Darussalam (BND 50.00 deposit fee; counter payments accepted Monday to Thursday and Saturday mornings), and instruments signed abroad must be notarized in the country of origin [3].
  • Land Code requirements and incapacity limits: Powers covering land transactions must also satisfy the Land Code (Chapter 40); ordinary agency authority does not override later court mental-capacity controls [3][4].
  • Mental Health Order protections: Where an ill person loses mental capacity without settled financial arrangements, applications and safeguards are governed under the Mental Health Order, 2014 listed by Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) Brunei Darussalam, making early joint-bill delegation and clear banking instructions essential [4].

steps.title: SPK Terminal Illness and Incapacitation Withdrawals
steps.html:
• SPK Terminal Illness Withdrawal: Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP) allows eligible members under the National Retirement Scheme (SPK) to apply for SPK Terminal Illness Withdrawal or SPK Incapacitation Withdrawal via the e-Amanah portal once qualifying medical documentation is submitted [5][6].
  • SPK Age 55+ and Silver Generation rules: Check whether your family member transitioned to SPK or belongs to the Silver Generation cohort (born 1968 to 1973 who deferred conversion) remaining under legacy TAP/SCP withdrawal rules, and review FAQ criteria via Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP) [5][6][7].
  • Registering an Administrator Nominee on e-Amanah: Appoint up to three Administrator Nominees and record next-of-kin details on e-Amanah while the member has capacity; TAP disburses SPK balances directly to the registered Administrator Nominee (who holds a legal duty to distribute fairly under Faraid or a valid will) and a separate will or Hibah declaration does not replace an e-Amanah Administrator Nomination [5].

steps.title: Wills, Syariah Faraid alignment, and Hague Apostilles
steps.html:
• Dual-system will and succession planning: Non-Muslim residents can execute a written will compliant with the Wills Act (Chapter 193) for administration by Probate Office of the High Court (Judiciary of Brunei Darussalam), whereas Muslim residents should align any Wasiat or Hibah planning with Islamic inheritance (Faraid) under the Islamic Family Law Act (Chapter 217), because probate grants for Muslim estates require a Syariah Court Faraid Order [8][9][10].
  • Organizing property and banking records: Gather land titles, bank mandates, insurance policies, and foreign asset statements alongside identity and family certificates managed with Immigration and National Registration Department (INRD) so probate or Summary Grant eligibility (under BND 25,000) and civil-document authenticity are clear [2][8][11].
  • Hague Apostille for overseas assets: Because Brunei is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, powers of attorney, certified identity records, or notarized statements executed in Brunei for overseas banks or registries can be certified with an Apostille (BND 2.00) by Supreme Court of Brunei Darussalam [12].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Brunei. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Brunei for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health (MOH) Brunei Darussalam
contacts.note: Oversees public hospitals, geriatric and palliative care services, and Bru-HIMS health records in Brunei.

contacts.name: Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) Brunei Darussalam
contacts.note: Operates the Registry of Powers of Attorney (BND 50.00 deposit fee) and publishes Brunei statutes including the Mental Health Order.

contacts.name: Tabung Amanah Pekerja (TAP)
contacts.note: Administers SPK Terminal Illness Withdrawal, SPK Incapacitation Withdrawal, and e-Amanah Administrator Nominee registration.

contacts.name: Probate Office of the High Court (Judiciary of Brunei Darussalam)
contacts.note: Administers civil Grants of Probate, Letters of Administration, and Summary Administration for intestate estates not exceeding BND 25,000.

contacts.name: Supreme Court of Brunei Darussalam
contacts.note: Designated Article 6 Competent Authority issuing 1961 Hague Apostilles (BND 2.00 fee).
